Minimal fix: treat unparseable comparands as not equal.

This is the numpy-2 copy-keyword incompatibility. Shimming that is deeper — `np.array(..., copy=False)` appears in many places in old astropy.

That's hacky but works at runtime: wrap numpy.array so that when copy=False, call np.asarray(obj, ...) with subok/order/like handled. Actually np.asarray doesn't accept subok? It does: np.asarray(a, dtype, order, like, subok?) — np.asarray has no subok param... Actually `np.asarray(a, dtype=None, order=None, *, like=None)` — no subok. But `np.array(obj, copy=False, subok=True)` ≡ `np.asarray(obj, subok=True)`? np.asarray signature: np.asarray(a, dtype=None, order=None, *, like=None) — hmm, in numpy 2, np.asarray does have subok? So np.array(obj, copy=False, subok=True) ≡ np.asanyarray(obj, dtype=dtype, order=order).

In numpy 2, np.array(obj, copy=None) means "copy only if needed" — exactly numpy 1's copy=False behavior! From the migration guide: "copy=False" in numpy 2 raises if a copy is needed; copy=None copies when needed. So the clean shim: wrap np.array and map copy=False → copy=None. np.array = _array
